pr_title: Add `tootctl domains purge` options to select subdomains and keep domain blocks
pr_body:
Fixes #21984

- Add a `--include-subdomains` option to match both passed domains and their subdomains
- Add support for the `*.` subdomain wildcard pattern regardless of `--include-subdomains` as people will somewhat frequently use it
- Fix issues with custom emoji deletion
- Change `tootctl domains purge` to not remove domain blocks by default, and add a `--purge-domain-blocks` option to recover that behavior: in most cases, if a domain block exists, admins do not actually want to remove it.

issue_context.title: `tootctl domains purge` does not include subdomains, while instance blocks do
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Run `tootctl domains purge`, eg on the recent spam domain activitypub-troll.cf 
2. Observe that no subdomains are purged.
...


### Expected behaviour

Domain blocks extend to subdomains, so purges should, too (or at least have an option to disable that mode)

### Actual behaviour

Subdomains do not get purged.

### Detailed description

Only the exact match is purged. In the case of the recent spam domain, this sucks – we have over 1k individual 1 user spam domains lying around now, and no real way to get rid of them.

### Specifications

Mastodon 4.0.2
comments: This extends to the purge button in the admin UI if you only suspend an apex domain and then purge it.

This should be an explicit flag, though, both in the admin UI (maybe a checkbox) and on the CLI. You usually only want to purge the apex domain (old entries of instances that have moved to a new subdomain, etc.).

review_comments: `subdomain_patterns` is defined in an `if`, and then you try to do `subdomain_patterns +=`. If `include_subdomains` were true and `domain` didn't start with `*.`, wouldn't this error?
Oh, the `if` is inside the `filter_map` block. Nevermind! :D
The `if` is in the `filter_map`! If nothing matches, `subdomain_patterns` is an empty array, not `nil`
